steps.title: Foothills of the Andes
steps.body: Alto Maipo, upper Maipo, is the eastern part of the valley, in the Andean foothills, at about 600 to 900 m. Areas include Puente Alto, Pirque and Buin. It's cooler than the valley floor, with strong mountain breezes and a big day and night swing.

steps.title: Soils and style
steps.body: Soils are alluvial, with stones, gravel and clay, washed down from the Andes by the Maipo river. They drain well and limit vigour. Alto Maipo Cabernet is more structured and elegant than the valley floor's, with blackcurrant, mint, graphite and fine tannins. It's often compared with Bordeaux's Left Bank.

steps.prompt: Why is Alto Maipo Cabernet more structured than valley floor Cabernet?
options: Cooler foothill sites and stony soils

steps.title: Puente Alto
steps.body: Puente Alto, on an ancient river terrace, is home to some of Chile's most famous Cabernet vineyards: Don Melchor's vineyard, Almaviva and Viñedo Chadwick. Viñedo Chadwick topped a 2004 Berlin tasting, a Chilean version of the Judgment of Paris, ahead of top Bordeaux.

steps.explanation: Casablanca is a separate coastal valley.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Alto Maipo sits in the Andean foothills
Stony soils and cool air give structured Cabernet
Puente Alto is home to Chile's icon Cabernets
